editor.canvasHint: Drag objects to move them; drag the top-right square to resize. White dot: horizon height, blue dot: tilt, red dots: vanishing points.

toolbar.clearBody: Removes all figures and scenery and resets the horizon and perspective. You can restore it with Undo.

horizon.hint: On flat ground the horizon crosses every person at the camera height (eye-level rule). Use “Snap to eye level” on a figure to get a consistent size.

perspective.hint: Vanishing points always sit on the horizon. Buildings are drawn converging to them.

inspector.none: Tap an object on the canvas to edit it here.

help.title: Help
help.intro: Composition Explorer lets you design and explore compositions — horizon, perspective, figures and scenery — as drafts for AI illustration.

sections.title: Getting started
items: Use the panels on the left (below on phones) to set the canvas ratio, horizon and perspective.
Add figures and scenery, then drag them on the canvas.
Drag the square at the top-right of the selection to resize.
Export as PNG / SVG / JSON. JSON files can be re-imported.
Your work is saved in the browser automatically. “Clear” starts over (undo is available).

sections.title: Horizon and camera
items: Horizon height corresponds to camera tilt; its angle is the camera roll (Dutch angle).
Drag the white handle on the left for height and the blue handle on the right for tilt.
With a camera height, the eye-level rule computes a natural figure size from where it stands.

sections.title: Perspective
items: 1-point: receding lines meet at one vanishing point — roads, corridors, frontal buildings.
2-point: two vanishing points — looking at the corner of a building. Closer VPs mean stronger perspective.
Buildings are drawn in 3D following the vanishing points.

sections.title: Composition guides
items: Overlay the rule of thirds, golden section, diagonals, center lines and the golden spiral.
Guides are only guides — breaking them on purpose can be powerful.

sections.title: Saving and reproducibility
sections.body: JSON files include a schema version and random seed so compositions can be reproduced exactly. Exploration will be reproducible from the same conditions and seed as well.

sections.title: Coming next
items: Phase 2: mathematical evaluation (thirds, golden ratio, visual balance, negative space…)
Phase 3: parallel exploration in Web Workers presenting 10 diverse candidates (Masterpiece ⇔ Discovery slider)
Phase 4: re-exploration from a chosen composition, mutation, favorites
Phase 5: richer AI-oriented exports and a Google Colab edition

about.title: About
about.tagline: Learn from masterpieces, discover unseen compositions.
about.philosophyBody: Theories like the golden ratio or rule of thirds are guides for evaluating a composition, not guarantees of beauty. Composition Explorer does not impose a single right answer: it respects classical theory while valuing the compositions that lie beyond it.
about.referencesHint: Ideas are referenced; no code from papers is used — everything is implemented independently.
